newsitem.title: USA: Dominican sugar seen at 655,000 tonnes- US attache.
newsitem.headline: Dominican sugar seen at 655,000 tonnes- US attache.

text.p: Sugar production in the Dominican Republic is expected to increase 10 to 15 pct to more than 655,000 tonnes in marketing year 1997, weather permitting, a U.S. attache in Santo Domingo said.
In a report made public on Tuesday, the U.S. attache said Dominican sugar output was 590,000 tonnes in 1996 and 482,000 tonnes in 1995.

Decreases in raw sugar production at the state-owned Consortium Estatal del Azucar (CEA), which mostly poroduces sugar for the U.S. export market, have been offset by production increases at both privately-owned mills, Central Romana and Vicini, the report said. Central Romana has also continued to use its expanded refinery capacity to fill shortfalls in refined sugar availability created by the closure of CEA's Porvenir refinery.
"While it is still early in the season, an extended dry spell is currently affecting many sugar producing lands, and, if it continues, will adversely affect next year's production," the report said.
The Caribbean nation should be able to meet its 1997 quota, whether it remains at the current level of 321,000 tonnes or increased to about 355,000 tonnes, the report said.
U.S. attache reports are not considered official U.S. Agriculture Department data.
